name: Codex CLI

allow.note: Only deny is enforced on PreToolUse. An allow is accepted and changes nothing — the call proceeds to Codex's own approval logic. Allow is only enforced on PermissionRequest.

deny.note: Works in every mode including --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox. A deny with a blank reason is rejected as invalid, so the reason string is load-bearing.

ask.note: There is no ask verdict in any mode. On PreToolUse, permissionDecision 'ask' is parsed, rejected as invalid, and the call then runs anyway. LeastGrant converts a floored ask into a deny where no human can be reached.

onCrash.note: Every failure path sets HookRunStatus::Failed and leaves the call to proceed.

timeoutDefaultSeconds.note: SessionEnd and Interrupt default to 1s and are hard-clamped.

firesOnFailure.note: PostToolUse fires only when the tool call succeeded (`if success` in the registry), so LeastGrant never observes a failed call and cannot learn that something was refused.

canModifyInput.note: updatedInput on PreToolUse, last handler to complete wins. LeastGrant does not use it.

modes.askSurvivesNote: Nothing. permission_mode is derived only from the approval policy and never from the sandbox mode, so `default` does not imply a human will be asked. `codex exec` hard-sets the policy to Never.

upstreamLimitations: No ask verdict exists at all. On Codex, LeastGrant is a veto rather than a prompt.

A handler declared `"async": true` cannot apply control effects: its deny, its exit-2 block and its updatedInput are all silently ignored. A single wrong word in the config is a total, unsignalled bypass.
Hook trust is bound to a hash of the definition, so upgrading or reinstalling re-flags the hook and it stops running until re-trusted in /hooks.
On Windows the trust hash covers only `commandWindows` and on POSIX only `command`, so one hooks.json has different hashes on different machines.
`codex exec` has no trust review and no warning: an untrusted or modified handler is simply never added to the handler set, and nothing says so.
Fails open on crash and on timeout.
`[features] hooks = false` and `allow_managed_hooks_only = true` disable user hooks entirely.
leastgrantLimitations: PermissionRequest has never fired in a real session. `codex exec` runs unattended, where by definition nothing prompts, so that path is contract-tested only.

live.what: Real `codex exec` sessions driven end to end: a credential read and a write to LeastGrant’s own records were both blocked, while `node --version` and `git status` ran untouched.

transport.what: Codex runs hook commands through PowerShell on Windows; the quoting failure that made the hook never start was found by watching a real session print "PreToolUse Failed" and run the command anyway.

contract.what: Events, payload fields, decision parsing and the four kill switches read from the shipped codex.exe and codex-rs sources.

mechanism: Command handlers for `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest` and `PostToolUse` in ~/.codex/hooks.json. Codex binds trust to a hash of the handler definition, so upgrading re-flags it until re-trusted in /hooks.
